subject: the design of a stadium, as part of Phase II of Willets Point, 126th Street, 127th Street, and Willets Point Boulevard between 38th Avenue and 35th Avenue, Corona, Queens
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the design of a stadium, as part of Phase II of Willets Point, 126th Street, 127th Street, and Willets Point Boulevard between 38th Avenue and 35th Avenue, Corona, Queens, submitted by the Economic Development Corporation, represented by exhibits 7716-AN, AO, AP, AQ & AR of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will provide in an interim submission before returning for final review, (1) heat island studies, considering the impact of materials proposed for the ground plane and for the building; (2) alternatives to the material palette, considering whether the design intent to provide contrast through the material palette can be achieved through (a) the use of dark metal panels selectively as an architectural accent, rather than as a broad façade treatment, or (b) the use of a lighter landscape palette to contrast with the building; (3) elevations with all material options rendered; (4) plan diagrams of signage, distinguishing between instances of branding signage versus wayfinding signage; (5) an update on the plan for public art and public selection process, including (a) whether the team will follow the Percent for Art program, (b) whether artwork can be sited in a way that is more visible, welcoming and integrated with communal spaces, and (c) further details on how the artwork is intended to be experienced at the human scale; and (6) studies exploring how the communal spaces will be occupied, and inviting and welcoming for all uses on non-game days. Commissioner Tisch recused herself. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before May 20, 2026 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the restoration of the Bethesda Fountain including conservation of Angel of the Waters (1873) by Emma Stebbins, Central Park, 72nd Street Drive, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation and the Central Park Conservancy, represented by exhibits 554-AL, AM, AN, AO, AP & AQ of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) schedule a site visit with the Conservation Advisory Group members to review physical mock-ups of the bronze treatments, including studies of (a) the recasting and repatination and (b) patching; (2) provide further details on the modeling methods for casting the decorative bronze elements, including to (a) clarify whether modeling will be done by hand or digitally, (b) confirm whether the team has the original molds for casting, (c) clarify who will be responsible for the modeling and recasting work, and (d) provide additional drawings of the missing decorative elements; (3) provide further details on the proposed water flow at the fountain, including whether there are any proposed spout alterations; (4) study adding educational signage explaining the history of the fountain and the Angel of the Waters sculpture; and (5) clarify the intent of the digital scanning and explain how the scanning process related to prior treatments of the bronze elements. subject: the reconstruction of Third Street Playground, Prospect Park, Prospect Park West between 3rd Street and 4th Street, adjacent to West Drive, Brooklyn
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of Third Street Playground, Prospect Park, Prospect Park West between 3rd Street and 4th Street, adjacent to West Drive, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation and the Prospect Park Alliance, represented by exhibits 3978-N, O, P, Q & R of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) expand the paved area beneath the benches to provide clear circulation around the mounds, ensuring users don’t need to walk on the turf; (2) restudy the circulation to the west of the swings to allow users to access the benches comfortably, without interfering with children at play; and (3) simplify the design of the wooden deck to better integrate with the overall site geometry and facilitate easier construction. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before January 21, 2027, and submission of this project for final review and approval.

subject: the reconstruction of Harding Park, Bolton Avenue and Gildersleeve Avenue, Bronx
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of Harding Park, Bolton Avenue and Gildersleeve Avenue, Bronx, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 5788-F, G, H, I & J of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) provide seating areas for larger group gatherings; (2) consider installing edging around the garden beds or signage to clearly delineate the landscape areas and pathways, preserve the woodlands, and prevent users from creating desire paths, particularly in the northern parcel; (3) provide a site horticulture maintenance strategy to ensure the eradication of the invasive plant species, ideally before construction begins; (4) consider a design for the basketball court paving that reflects the local culture; and (5) consider installing non-mechanical sound elements into the play equipment that mimic the sound of coqui frogs. The Commission commended the project, appreciating its strong site design that seamlessly connects various activities, while preserving the existing woodlands. Commissioners also appreciated the team’s collaboration with local communities to incorporate cultural elements into the playground that are both inclusive and playful. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before January 21, 2027, and submission of this project for final review and approval.

subject: the design of a master plan for the construction of Metropolitan Park (Queens Future), including the construction of a gaming facility, resort, retail, and events complex, parking structures, the reconstruction of Shea Road, and adjacent site work, Roosevelt
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the design of a master plan for the construction of Metropolitan Park (Queens Future), including the construction of a gaming facility, resort, retail, and events complex, parking structures, the reconstruction of Shea Road, and adjacent site work, Roosevelt, submitted by the Economic Development Corporation and the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 7786-E, F, G, H & I of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval, subject to the conditions listed below. Commissioner Castilla recused herself. Commissioner Armstead voted to abstain, citing too many unknowns. This approval is conditioned upon the following requests for design development and clarifications, which must be included in amended preliminary submissions prior to proceeding to final review: (1) For the Integrated Resort: (a) mitigate the public space impact from the approximately 50 relocated parking spots on Roosevelt Avenue, potentially redistributing the spaces away from the pedestrian frontage; (b) continue to design the daycare center, including the façade treatment and the access and design details of the outdoor playground, including how this space interfaces with the adjacent public realm; (c) provide information on the proposed smoking terrace and cigar bar, including how their impacts can be mitigated at major public access points and gathering spaces; (d) continue the design development of the mezzanine- level promenade at the east colonnade, particularly as it relates to accessible circulation; and the (e) continue to study the design of the northern surface lot, including to reduce the quantity of garage entrances, to rationalize vehicle circulation, and to mitigate the impacts from the one- way bus and loading route exit on Metropolitan Park. (2 & 3) For the Northfield Garage and Southfield Garage: (a) refine the ground plane design, including to provide additional activated façades and fencing details, especially at the interface with the Willets Point neighborhood; and (b) at both the Metropolitan Park and Seaver Way locations, continue to refine the circulation lobbies and elevated connection spaces, considering the public interface and anti-climb features.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of To Fly by Tatyana Fazlalizadeh, Horizon Juvenile Center, 560 Brooke Avenue, Bronx, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Administration for Children's Services, represented by exhibits 6064-BO, BP, BQ & BR of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that the artist will (1) consider the legibility of the text element from different vantage points, including how the scale and location of the text relates to the intended audience and (2) coordinate with the design team to (a) ensure that the proposal reflects the latest building and site design, (b) study additional views of the artwork from different vantage points, such as from within the recreation field, and (c) ensure that the lighting at this wall is adequate, noting that the team could consider additional lighting on the canopy, if necessary. RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of a marker (First Portable Cell Phone Call), Sixth Avenue between West 53rd Street and West 54th Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 7609-A, D & E of record in this matter, hereby rejects the same, noting that while there was a press event for the first public portable cell phone call that took place on a New York City sidewalk, the phone was not invented in New York City and the event has minimal relevancy to the City. Commissioners also noted concern with the proliferation of markers and setting precedent. Some commissioners supported and celebrated the commemoration of the event and appreciated the team’s responsiveness to feedback on the design. Commissioners Castilla, Miranda, Tisch, and Van Bramer approved the project.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of astros by Ronny Quevedo, southwest corner of Queens Boulevard and Woodhaven Boulevard, as part of the reconstruction of Queens Boulevard, Elmhurst, Queens, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 7388-S, T, U & V of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that in an interim submission prior to returning for preliminary review, the artist will (1) for the site context and streetscape improvements, (a) coordinate with the Department of Transportation and the capital project team to provide further details about the streetscape improvements that will be made to the site and (b) provide drawings and/or diagrams that show the artwork within the context of the capital project improvements; (2) for maintenance and safety, (a) further study and provide an update on methods to deter potential climbing of the sculpture, (b) provide further details about the maintenance plan, depending on how the artwork is further developed, (c) consider closing the top face of the open-top crate that has a basketball beneath it to prevent debris accumulation or other objects from getting stuck in that area; and (3) for viewer participation and interaction, (a) consider how the artwork can serve as social infrastructure that promotes interaction between a diverse range of participants who may engage with it at varying frequencies (i.e. daily, weekly, or as a one-time visitor) and who might develop a sense of ownership over the artwork and site, creating a living functionality that evolves with community engagement, (b) further study how the artwork responds to the needs and desires of the surrounding community and the intended use of the site, and (c) consider whether the artwork can create a calming space in an otherwise busy and highly trafficked area. Conceptual approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for preliminary review and approval before April 28, 2027.

subject: the construction of a greenway and daylighting of Tibbetts Brook, between West 230th Street and Hester and Piero’s Mill Pond, Van Cortlandt Park, Bronx
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the construction of a greenway and daylighting of Tibbetts Brook, between West 230th Street and Hester and Piero’s Mill Pond, Van Cortlandt Park, Bronx, submitted by the Department of Environmental Protection and the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 1960-EB, EC, ED, EE, EF, EG & EH of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that prior to returning for final review, the team will (1) holistically refine the architectural elements along the greenway to make the space feel recognizable as a truly public, pedestrianized space, including by (a) reconsidering the suitability of the Davit pole for a pedestrian and cycling path, (b) considering the cohesion, detailing, and transparency of the railing design, decking, and gates across all different site widths and landscape types, particularly where the path is narrow and the railing could feel heavy, opaque, or constricting, and (c) thinking about the architectural identity and detailing along the length of the corridor and how it varies based on the width and context of the site; (2) update the presentation to provide (a) detailed cross sections showing the ways in which the structures, railings, lighting, furnishings, planting, and other elements relate to the varied site conditions along each segment of the project and (b) a phasing and construction sequencing diagram; (3) develop a signage strategy and graphic that pulls the design together across all of the landscape types and that (a) considers the experience of pedestrians accessing the greenway at different entry points and (b) relates to the NYC Parks graphic identity standards while also distinguishing itself as a unique greenway space; and (4) clarify the maintenance strategy further, including (a) whether the porous pavement will be regularly vacuumed, (b) whether a replanting budget can be reserved for the future, and (c) whether the design team can help NYC Parks and DEP to establish a maintenance guide for the site. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before August 14, 2025.

subject: the reconstruction of the bandshell and construction of an adjacent shade structure, as part of the reconstruction of Damrosch Park, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, West 62nd Street between Columbus Avenue and Amsterdam Avenue, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of the bandshell and construction of an adjacent shade structure, as part of the reconstruction of Damrosch Park, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, West 62nd Street between Columbus Avenue and Amsterdam Avenue, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation and the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 3470-HF, HG & HH of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that in a month, the team shall submit for interim review during the October 2025 project review cycle, provide responses and drawings that are responsive to the following conditions of approval, including to (1) continue to develop a unified language for the architectural elements in Damrosch Park, editing the design across the campus to simplify and reduce the disparate elements, materials, and geometries; (2) rethink the proportions and relationship of the bandshell canopy, the overlook trellis structure, and the steps to create a gateway into the plaza, and include (a) transverse and longitudinal sections through both, and (b) renderings from a pedestrian perspective to show how both structures are experienced simultaneously; (3) develop the design to allow spatial flexibility for equitable daily use, including to (a) study how to provide ADA access to the seating area at the southwest stoop to provide an equitable, elevated vantage point toward the park and street, (b) include ADA companion seating throughout, and (c) reduce any trip hazards and accessibility or circulation challenges at the overlook steps; (4) at the overlook trellis structure, (a) remove the tension cables and vines from the trellis, (b) redesign the trellis for improved shading for the seating beneath, (c) provide detailed drawings showing any control booths, audio-visual, and lighting equipment, and (d) provide seating diagrams that clearly illustrate circulation clearances and the relation of the seating area to the adjacent grove; (5) refine the West 62nd Street bandshell façade to create a more welcoming street wall condition and entrance into Damrosch Park, including to (a) investigate opportunities to provide public amenities with streetscape design elements and (b) consider allowing the tiered stoop seating to wrap the corner of the building along West 62nd Street to provide a more welcoming frontage toward the university campus; and (6) address additional site-specific feedback noted by commissioners, including but not limited to concerns that (a) the plaza needs to accommodate operational requirements for performances and everyday uses at all scales, (b) the deep cavity space under the proscenium stage needs to be resolved, and any panels or guardrails must be shown on drawings, (c) the complexity and heaviness of the bandshell roof needs to be further studied, lightened, and simplified, (d) any rooftop maintenance and safety

subject: the rehabilitation of Columbus Park Pavilion, Columbus Park, Worth Street, Baxter Street, Mulberry Street, and Bayard Street, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the rehabilitation of Columbus Park Pavilion, Columbus Park, Worth Street, Baxter Street, Mulberry Street, and Bayard Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 3974-AO, AP & AQ of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that, when returning for final review, the team will pursue a pavilion screening design that uses Option ‘D’ (with no upper ‘X’) for the panels and either Option ‘B’ (with an upper ‘X’ at the door) or Option ‘D’ (with no upper ‘X’ at the door) for the design of the doors, and (1) consider using as transparent and lightweight a mesh as possible, and including a physical sample for review; (2) study how the entry doors fit within the design of the arched opening; (3) reduce the mullion size to be as slim as possible, to lighten both the visual and physical weight; and (4) reduce the weight of the doors as much as possible and use robust hinges to prevent future sagging and maintenance or operations challenges. Commissioners thanked the team for its responsiveness to past feedback and its efforts to propose a design that will be more transparent and require less daily maintenance than roll gates would have required. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before September 16, 2026, and submission of this project for final review and approval.

subject: the reconstruction of a plaza (Canal Street Triangle) as part of the Gateways to Chinatown program, Walker Street, Baxter Street, and Canal Street, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of a plaza (Canal Street Triangle) as part of the Gateways to Chinatown program, Walker Street, Baxter Street, and Canal Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 6617-Q, R & S of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous final approval with the understanding that (1) the Commission discourages the proliferation of digital signs in the public realm in general, and particularly in parks and similar places intended for the enjoyment of nature and/or historic sites; (2) a digital sign in this location will not negatively change the experience of the plaza; (3) the digital content will be limited to (a) artistic, historic, and cultural content that will be curated by the DOT Art Program in collaboration with a neighborhood cultural institution and (b) sponsorship opportunities will be limited to no more than 10% of the screen and overseen by the Chinatown Partnership Business Improvement District (BID), which will also maintain the plaza; (4) DOT will provide clarification on when the WalkNYC map can be adapted for other frames and contexts; (5) the team will revise the kiosk design by (a) replacing the cylindrical rods with a more durable and less climbable option, such as cables and (b) raising the kiosk structure from the ground for ease of maintenance; and (6) by Fall 2021, the team will submit an updated proposal with the revised kiosk, including (a) final drawings, (b) details on the digital screen resolution, size, and illumination, durability, content management plan and system, maintenance and warranties, life-cycle, and any other feedback from the consultant, and (c) a draft of the maintenance agreement, including a detailed plan for the management of the digital screen. Commissioner Marton recused herself. Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before May 24, 2023 and submission of comprehensive photographic documentation of the completed project consisting of 8” x 10” archival-quality color photographs.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the long term loan of Thomas Jefferson (1833) by Pierre-Jean David (David D'Angers), City Council Chamber, City Hall to the New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, represented by exhibits 793-H & I of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval to the removal of the artwork from the City Council Chamber with the understanding that the location will be further studied and, before the end of 2021, an appropriate location will be determined where it will remain accessible to the public. The Commission notes the history of the artwork in City Hall, that it was gifted to the people of New York by one of the first Jewish officers in the U.S. military, Uriah Phillips Levy, in recognition of Thomas Jefferson’s commitment to religious freedom, and that Jefferson was the author of the Declaration of Independence, a founding document of the United States. The Commission also recognizes the layered narratives and meanings assigned to this artwork and takes seriously the implications of monumentalizing figures who, despite espousing the virtues of freedom and democracy, prospered from the labor of enslaved people and upheld racist beliefs to justify the institution of slavery. The Commission acknowledges the passionate call from members of the City Council to remove the artwork from their chambers and to install it in a place where it can be contextualized and serve as an educational tool. The Commission also thanks the New-York Historical Society for its ongoing commitment to providing opportunities for the public to learn about and discuss the history of New York City and the Country.

subject: the reconstruction of the Kinderberg, restoration of the Chess and Checkers House, and adjacent site work, East 65th Street transverse road between Center Drive and East Drive, Central Park, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of the Kinderberg, restoration of the Chess and Checkers House, and adjacent site work, East 65th Street transverse road between Center Drive and East Drive, Central Park, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation and the Central Park Conservancy, represented by exhibits 2948-T, U, V & W of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that (1) the Landmarks Preservation Commission has binding jurisdiction over the proposed work on the Chess and Checkers House; (2) no concession is planned for the site; (3) alternate locations for the ramp were studied and the one proposed was determined to (a) result in the least amount of disturbance of the landscape and (b) provide the most equitable accessible route for people with diverse mobilities; (4) bluestone with a thermal finish will be used on the ramp walls, noting that the ramp is designed to be clearly identified as a contemporary intervention; and (5) the number of railings and guardrails do not exceed those specified by code. The Commission notes the Central Park Conservancy’s thorough research into its proposals and acknowledges the challenge of designing contemporary interventions within Central Park in a way that respects the different periods of historic significance while meeting current codes and serving the public. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before February 14, 2024.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the removal and temporary storage of Enlightenment and Arms of the City of New York (1940) by Rene Paul Chambellan, Manhattan Detention Complex, 125 White Street, White Street between Baxter Street and Centre Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Design and Construction and the Department of Correction, represented by exhibits 4724-AP, AQ, AR & BE of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that a proposal for the conservation and re-installation of the artworks, including a maintenance plan, will be submitted for review as part of the proposal for the new facility at the same site. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before February 14, 2024 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the removal and temporary storage of The Judgement of Pao Kung and The Judgement of Solomon (1989) by Richard Haas, Manhattan Detention Complex, 125 White Street, Baxter Street façade, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Correction, represented by exhibits 4724-AS, AT, AU & BE of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) work with the artist to develop a proposal to conserve and reinstall the artworks at the new jail facility or another appropriate location approved by the artist; (2) submit a plan and schedule for this work, taking into consideration the age of the artists and the expedited design-build timeline for the new facility; and (3) provide a plan for how the Department of Correction will ensure that these and other artworks installed under its jurisdiction will be maintained as originally installed. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before February 14, 2024 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the removal of Immigration on the Lower East Side of New York (1989) by Richard Haas, Manhattan Detention Complex, 125 White Street, Baxter Street façade, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Correction, represented by exhibits 4724-AV, AW, AX & BE of record in this matter, hereby rejects the same. The Commission expresses support and respect for the artist and their work and is disheartened by the lack of maintenance for all the artworks at the site. The Commission acknowledges the infeasibility of salvaging the existing artwork, which is painted directly onto the building’s exterior wall, but notes the importance of preserving artworks that represent immigrants and people of color as part of the history of New York City. The Commission requests that the team (1) transform the artwork from the existing corporeal form to a digital form; (2) work with the artist to develop a proposal to share the artwork with the public either at the new jail facility or another appropriate location approved by the artist; (3) submit a plan and schedule for the work outlined above, taking into consideration the age of the artist and the expedited design-build timeline for the new facility; and (4) provide a plan for how the Department of Correction will ensure that these and other artworks installed under its jurisdiction will be maintained as installed.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the removal and temporary storage of The Seven Columns of the Temple of Wisdom and Solomon’s Throne (1992) by Kit-Yin Snyder, Manhattan Detention Complex, White Street between Baxter Street and Centre Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Correction represented by exhibits 4724-AY, AZ, BA & BE of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) work with the artist to develop a proposal to conserve and reinstall the artworks at the new jail facility or another appropriate location approved by the artist; (2) submit a plan and schedule for this work, taking into consideration the age of the artists and expedited design-build timeline for the new facility; and (3) provide a plan for how the Department of Correction will ensure that these and other artworks installed under its jurisdiction will be maintained as originally installed. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before February 14, 2024 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the removal of Upright (1992) by Kit-Yin Snyder, Manhattan Detention Complex, White Street between Baxter Street and Centre Street, 125 White Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Correction, represented by exhibits 4724-BB, BC, BD & BE of record in this matter, hereby rejects the same. The Commission expresses support and respect for the artist and their work and is disheartened by the lack of maintenance for all the artworks at the site. The Commission requests that the team (1) work with the artist to develop a proposal to recreate the artwork at the new jail facility or another appropriate location approved by the artist; (2) submit a plan and schedule for this work, taking into consideration the age of the artist and expedited design-build timeline for the new facility; and (3) provide a plan for how the Department of Correction will ensure that these and other artworks installed under its jurisdiction will be preserved as installed.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of Memory of a Forest by Blane de St. Croix, Emergency Medical Station 17 (EMS 17), 1257 Morris Avenue, Bronx, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program and the Department of Design and Construction, represented by exhibits 636-K, L, M & N of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that the artist will (1) acknowledge the relationship of the Lenape people to the pre-European landscapes that are being shown in the artwork, potentially by (a) collaborating with an organization or historian with expertise in the subject to further develop the artwork concept and (b) adding didactic signage and a land acknowledgement that contextualizes the miniature landscape sculptures within the larger history of people who thrived within forested areas before European colonization transformed the landscape, and (2) pull inspiration from other surviving examples of old growth forests in the Bronx, such as Van Cortlandt Park. Conceptual approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for preliminary review and approval before June 21, 2023.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of Resonances by Christopher Myers, Brownsville Library, 61 Glenmore Avenue, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program and the Department of Design and Construction, represented by exhibits 2285-AJ, AK, AL & AM of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that (1) if the budget allows, the team will explore expanding the artwork into other areas of the library, potentially by adding a mural or incorporating the visual representations of magnetic resonance into other library elements and (2) the library will ensure that books written by or about the notable people depicted in the artworks are readily available to visitors. subject: the redesign of wayfinding and commemorative signage (Heritage Trails), Lower Manhattan, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the redesign of wayfinding and commemorative signage (Heritage Trails), Lower Manhattan, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Transportation on behalf of the Downtown Alliance, represented by exhibits 5789-F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N & O of record in this matter, hereby rejects the same. The Commission expressed appreciation for the work undertaken by the Downtown Alliance and the stated goals of providing more inclusive signage, noting that the Heritage Trail commemorative markers are an opportunity for truth and reconciliation and a pivotal opportunity to take a wider lens and accurately tell the history of the area, including stories on the Native American and enslaved populations. The Commission recommended that (1) the Heritage Trail signage program be holistically restudied; (2) the text, images, and locations be developed by a team of historical experts with relevant and diverse backgrounds of study; (3) additional signs be considered to commemorate significant historical persons or events as close as possible to the related locations; and (4) the revised text, images, and locations be shared in full with the community board before any resubmission to the Public Design Commission. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before June 21, 2023.

subject: the installation of a shade structure, Beach 59th Street Playground, Rockaway Beach, Shore Front Parkway between Beach 59th Street and Beach 60th Street, Arverne, Queens
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the installation of a shade structure, Beach 59th Street Playground, Rockaway Beach, Shore Front Parkway between Beach 59th Street and Beach 60th Street, Arverne, Queens, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 3402-L & M of record in this matter, notes that this project would ideally result in a family of modular structures of various shapes to accommodate different site layouts and provide greater shade coverage; however, given the agency’s limited schedule and budget, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the Department of Parks & Recreation will (1) work to minimize the structural elements as much as possible; (2) consider the use of aluminum and L- Beams; (3) revise the structure back to a rectangular shape if a family of structures is not possible; (4) increase the slope of the roof as previously shown or revise it to be flat; (5) continue to study the use and function of the solar units; (6) revise the shade structure layout plan, keeping in mind that the structures do not need to follow the curve of a path, but can be placed in a line over a path; and (6) integrate any security requirements into the site to minimize the need for bollards, in consultation with NYPD. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before April 15, 2021.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of an artwork by Kameelah Janan Rasheed, Willoughby Square Park, Willoughby Street, Abolitionist Place (Duffield Street) and Gold Street, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs’ Percent for Art Program and the Economic Development Corporation, represented by exhibits 5587-JF, JG, JH & JI of record in this matter, hereby tables the same. The Commission expresses support for the artist's work and robust community outreach plan, and notes the importance and challenge of creating a monumental memorial to the abolitionist movement in Brooklyn. The project may be resubmitted for review with the understanding that the artist will (1) work with the support of the landscape architect to identify additional artwork locations, including the site of the fountain, and to ensure the formal expressions of the artwork are prominent so the artwork becomes a focal point (or focal points) within the park; (2) consider legibility and long-term durability and maintenance of the text installations, in particular at locations where people will be sitting or walking; and (3) develop the content with input from community members, as proposed. Commissioner Aarons and Commissioner Armstead recused themselves.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a final report for the conservation of murals by Edwin Howland Blashfield, Kenyon Cox, Joseph Lauber, G.W. Maynard, William Metcalf, Henry Siddons Mowbray, Robert Reid, E. Simmons, Charles Y. Turner, and H. O. Walker, Appellate Courthouse, 35 East 25th Street at Madison Avenue, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Design and Construction and the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, represented by exhibits 2814-AS, AT & AU of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous final approval with the understanding that DCAS will implement the long- term maintenance program as recommended by the conservator in the report. Specifically, DCAS will (1) work with the Office of Court Administration to limit temperature and humidity fluctuations outside of the recommended ranges; (2) in 2027, schedule a fine art conservator to inspect the murals and provide a condition report with treatment recommendations; and (3) submit the report to the Public Design Commission along with the agency’s plan for implementing any recommendations.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of the Women's Rights Pioneers Monument by Meredith Bergmann, Literary Walk, The Mall, Central Park, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 7422- E, I & J of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that (1) this monument is not a precise historical truth but an artist’s allegorical depiction of a meeting that may have occurred at a specific moment in time before 1867; (2) the artist will (a) refine and emphasize the character, gestures, and faces of each of the figures in the full size model and (b) submit photographs of the full size model for review before the artwork is fabricated; (3) a graphic designer will lay out all of the text on the pedestal, including center-aligning all three women’s names and adjusting the kerning on the rear text as necessary, and the revised layout will be submitted for review before fabrication; and (4) the Monumental Women’s Statue Fund will develop an educational campaign with a website, apps, and events, and this campaign will include (a) an historically accurate telling of the complex and nuanced stories of the each of these three women and their role in the Women’s Rights Movement, which became divided and fractured after the 1867 American Equal Rights Association meeting due to racism and (b) an explanation of the artist’s concept and intent that clarifies that the depicted meeting is fictional. Commissioners Hawkinson, Valverde, and Willis Thomas abstained. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before October 21, 2021 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of the Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony Monument by Meredith Bergmann, Literary Walk, The Mall, Central Park, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 7422-A, B & D of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that (1) the artist will (a) work on refining the anatomy and proportions of each of the two figures, (b) restudy the gaze of the two women, (c) simplify the pedestal design so that the surface is flush, (d) eliminate the rectangular base or revise it to an oval to match the pedestal, and (e) integrate the bronze into the top of the base and (2) the team will submit revised pedestal text, including the birth and death dates for the two women and alternative quotes. The Commission appreciates that this monument will commemorate two women who were pioneering activists of the Woman Suffrage Movement. The Commission also acknowledges Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony's complicated history, and that the contributions and struggles of the many women of color who played a role in this Movement remain overlooked. With this in mind, the Commission gives approval conditioned upon the understanding that, separate from the statue of Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony, the applicant will work to identify meaningful ways to acknowledge and commemorate women of color who played an active role in the Woman Suffrage Movement. Conceptual approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for preliminary review and approval before March 18, 2021.

resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the construction of Buildings 2A and 2B and a central plaza as Phase II of the construction of four mixed-use residential towers, a light manufacturing facility, a central plaza open space, and adjacent site work (The Peninsula), Tiffany Street, Spofford Avenue and Manida Street, Bronx, submitted by the Economic Development Corporation, represented by exhibits 6544-CD, CF, CH, CI & CJ of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that, before returning for final review, the team will (1) continue to study the arrangement of windows at both buildings to ensure that the window placements are coordinated to bring visual interest to the facades but prioritized to serve the interior layouts of the individual units, specifically noting that (a) windows at bedrooms should be enlarged, (b) two adjacent vertical windows bands should be combined into a single larger window, and (c) the location of windows should be re-studied in coordination with developing an optimal floor plan that provides layout flexibility for residents and maximum light; (2) to ensure that window locations provide visual interest at the façade while also allowing for flexibility of interior layouts, submit examples of furniture layouts and floor plan alternatives; (3) provide details on the parapet cap and the tapered GFRC profile at the windows for Building 2B; and (4) submit diagrams illustrating how the hierarchy of design gestures was established, including how the massing, arrangement of fenestration, and material detailing relate to one another, noting that additional detail is needed to understand the relationship of the two gray metal panel colors on Building 2A, and of the window arrangement and GFRC taper at Building 2B . RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the temporary installation of Fearless Girl by Kristen Visbal, Broad Street between Wall Street and Exchange Place, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 7727-A, B & C of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same preliminary and final approval for the artwork to remain in its current location on Broad Street for eleven months, noting that this approval in no way constitutes an acceptance of the process leading up to the installation of the sculpture or of the piece as part of the City’s art collection. Approval is given with the understanding that the City will work with the artist and applicant and (1) within six months of the approval, provide an update on a substantive process in place to resolve the way in which this artwork will be adjudicated, placed, honored, and attributed to the artist and (2) the Department of Transportation will develop a policy with regard to works placed in the public realm without having gone through the proper process, so that such works are not allowed to remain. Commissioner Kiehl voted to table.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the deconstruction of Lighthouse and Bridge on Staten Island (1996) by Siah Armajani, North Shore Esplanade, adjacent to the Staten Island Ferry Terminal and former U.S. Coast Guard Light House Depot, Staten Island, submitted by the Department of Transportation and the Department of Cultural Affairs%, represented by exhibits 5623-R, S & T of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that (1) the artwork’s original fabrication has led to structural integrity issues; (2) the artwork has been closed since 2009 based on a structural engineer’s report; (3) since the artwork’s original installation, applicable laws, including the NYC Construction Codes have been updated and restoring the artwork now would require adding an elevator to meet applicable legal requirements, which would significantly alter the artist’s original vision; (4) DCLA and DOT will commission Siah Armajani to create a new artwork on the site; (5) the agencies have provided proof that funds have been established for the new artwork; (6) the artist has provided an email consenting to the removal of the artwork and agreeing to create a new artwork at the same site; (7) elements from the artwork, including the stained glass windows, will be carefully salvaged for future use by the artist in a new artwork; and (8) the artist has developed a conceptual proposal for the new artwork, which will be submitted for review in July 2017. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before June 19, 2019 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered the design of prototypical shrouds for 4G and 5G mobile telecommunications equipment for installation on light poles citywide, submitted by the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications and the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 6673-X & Y of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary and final approval only to the installations on the DOT Octagonal Pole, Type M-2A Signal Pole, Flatbush Avenue Pole, Alliance Pole (Type S), TBTA Pole, City Light, and 30’ Davit Pole, including the double-arm Davit Pole, but rejects the installations on the Bishop’s Crook and Type-M poles, including the double-arm Type-M pole. Approval is given with the understanding that (1) to ensure that installations prioritize underserved neighborhoods and the outer boroughs to bridge the digital divide, the team will (a) prior to any commencement of each new reservation phase, provide details on the total number of poles being released and percentages of distribution across each zone, noting that each phase will target greater than 75% of the poles in zones B and C and (b) also provide quarterly updates on the status of the installations; (2) the team will submit documentation from each community board confirming their review; (3) the team will study the inclusion of an integrated label or symbol to indicate to the public that these shrouds contain wireless infrastructure; (4) the color of the shrouds will always match the light pole; (5) only one set of shrouds will be allowed per pole; (6) if the technology changes during the lifetime of the franchise, the boxes will be made smaller and/or the antenna shorter, whenever possible; and (7) all sidewalks that are damaged during installation will be replaced-in-kind, per standard DOT and PDC review procedure. The Commission reiterates that franchisees should prioritize rooftop installations before light pole attachments and that all installations should be coordinated with appropriate agencies, including, but not limited to, the Landmarks Preservation Commission and Department of Parks and Recreation. Commissioner Nielsen abstains. Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before August 10, 2022 and submission of comprehensive photographic documentation of the completed project consisting of 8” x 10” archival-quality color photographs.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered the installation of prototypical public communications structures (Link5G) in Residence Zoning and Historic Districts citywide, submitted by the Office of Technology and Innovation, represented by exhibits 6816-IY, IZ & JA of record in this matter, hereby gives unanimous preliminary and final approval. Approval is given with the understanding that the installations will be limited to a fixed number of pilot sites and that the team will (1) submit a detailed pilot proposal for approval, which will include a specified cap on the number of installations as well as location as soon as possible or on an ongoing basis when known, and siting guidelines of the poles; (2) (a) engage community leaders before installation to ensure that they are aware of the proposal, including the design of the poles and provisioning of service, and are given an opportunity to provide feedback, and (b) continue to work with the Commission to identify ways to gauge community acceptance of structures installed and activated as part of the pilot; (3) provide local and/or global examples of multi-tenant 5G pole structures sited on sidewalks in comparable dense urban neighborhoods with the goal of suggesting alternatives for Residence Zoning and Historic Districts; and (4) remove and replace the pilot installations in the event another design is selected for citywide installation in Residence Zoning and Historic Districts. The Commission recognizes the urgency and need for internet access in underserved areas. Final approval is conditioned upon submission of a proposal for a fixed number of sites before August 8, 2024.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of the Women's Rights Pioneers Monument by Meredith Bergmann, Literary Walk, The Mall, Central Park, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 7422-E, F, G & H of record in this matter, hereby tables the same without prejudice to a resubmission provided the team provide all standard materials and responses to all previously provided feedback, including (1) letters from all relevant community boards; (2) written statements of support from independent historians who have expertise in the life and work of Sojourner Truth and who have seen the proposal, specifically noting their feedback on (a) the positions of the figures and their gestures in relation to one another, (b) the depicted ages of the figures, and (c) the estimated timeframe for the depiction; (3) refining the figures, including facial expressions, anatomical definition, and bodily postures; (4) revising the granite plinth from a rectangle to an oval; (5) restudying the alignment of the names on the pedestal; and (6) providing a layout of the rear pedestal text.

resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of the coastline (East Side Coastal Resiliency) and East River Park, including the construction of three bridges, a comfort station, two recreation centers, and two gate houses, East River between Montgomery Street and East 25th Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Design and Construction, the Department of Parks & Recreation, the Department of Environmental Protection, and the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 7368- J, K, L, M, N & O of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that the team will (1) re-study the alignment of the pedestrian bridge arches, noting that the previous angle was a more successful design and an integrated lighting solution would be warranted for three new bridges; (2) clarify the shade strategy for East River Park, including the caliper and projected growth of new trees; (3) incorporate more nuance into the wall pattern, in particular at the pedestrian scale; (4) include solatubes to bring natural light into the park buildings; (5) provide technical details on the glass brick gate house designs; (6) develop the closure gate design as part of the graphic designer’s scope and from the public’s perspective; and (7) provide a detailed design for the East River Park amphitheater, ensuring that it is accessible and functional. The Commission encouraged the team to continue to study the possibility of phasing the construction and thoughtfully consider any interim design solutions. Commissioner Nielsen recused herself. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before September 16, 2021.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered nominations for the positions of President, Vice President, and Secretary of the Design Commission, held a public vote. For the office of President, Deborah Marton was elected by Kenseth Armstead, Isabel Castilla, Laurie Hawkinson, Bill Heinzen, Karen Kiehl, Manuel Miranda, Susan Morgenthau, Merryl Tisch, Mary Valverde (voted remotely due to artist residency), and Jimmy Van Bramer. Deborah Marton abstained. As a result, Deborah Marton was elected President with ten in favor. For the office of Vice President, Kenseth Armstead and Jimmy Van Bramer were nominated. Isabel Castilla, Bill Heinzen, Karen Kiehl, Manuel Miranda, Susan Morgenthau, Merryl Tisch, and Jimmy Van Bramer voted in favor of electing Jimmy Van Bramer. Laurie Hawkinson, Mary Valverde (voted remotely due to artist residency), and Kenseth Armstead voted in favor of electing Kenseth Armstead. Deborah Marton abstained. As a result, Jimmy Van Bramer was elected Vice President with seven in favor, three against, and one abstention. For the office of Secretary, Isabel Castilla and Manuel Miranda were nominated. Kenseth Armstead, Laurie Hawkinson, Bill Heinzen, Karen Kiehl, Susan Morgenthau, Merryl Tisch, Mary Valverde (voted remotely due to artist residency), and Manuel Miranda voted in favor of electing Manuel Miranda. Isabel Castilla, Jimmy Van Bramer, and Deborah Marton abstained. As a result, Manuel Miranda was elected Secretary with seven in favor, and three abstentions.

subject: the reconstruction of the Upper Vale, including construction of the Northeast Pavilion, Prospect Park, Flatbush Avenue between Grand Army Plaza and the Prospect Park Zoo, Brooklyn

subject: the reconstruction of a community center, 70 Mulberry Street at Bayard Street, Manhattan
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of a community center, 70 Mulberry Street at Bayard Street, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Design and Construction and Department of Citywide Administrative Services represented by exhibits 6685-L, M, N, O, P & Q of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that before returning for final, the team will (1) at the façade (a) further clarify where BIPV and porcelain panels are being located, suggesting that Department of Citywide Adminstrative Services (DCAS) and the solar consultant be further engaged to ensure that the panel locations are optimized for maximum energy generation, (b) explore light-colored alternatives for the porcelain panels, noting that a dark, low- albedo tone is counterproductive to the team’s sustainability goals, and (c) clarify what material is being used at the location where the massing volume steps in; (2) further clarify (a) the window proportions, including fenestration details, (b) the function and detailing of the light wells and inset sills, (c) the detailing of the BIPV-integrated solar shade, and (d) how the prefabricated modular construction will impact and/or overlay with the fenestration locations; (3) provide an update on the forthcoming maintenance agreement with the DCAS, which should include a plan for panel maintenance or replacement that prevents an ad hoc appearance if BIPV panels lose functionality, noting that leaving defunct BIPV panels on the rainscreen is preferable to replacement with dark porcelain; and (4) continue to restudy the plant selections and adjacencies to address how (a) the sun-thriving understory species selected will survive under shaded trees, (b) the edible annual plants will be maintained, since they need to be replaced after they are harvested, and (c) the sedum will survive within planted areas with taller plants that require deeper soil depth, as these species do not typically mix well. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before July 17, 2025.

RESOLVED That the Art Commission, having considered a proposal for the conservation of Truth and Research, two plaster reliefs (ca. 1900) attributed to Herbert Adams and Olin L. Warner, Erasmus Hall High School, 911 Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn, submitted by the School Construction Authority, represented by exhibits 378-CK, CL & CM of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that, as the black paint may or may not be able to be removed without disturbing the original "bronze" finished surface, (1) tests, using various procedures and in various locations, be undertaken using cross sections to determine how much ofthe original frnish is below the black paint , if it is prudent to remove the black paint, and if so, what procedure(s) should be used to remove the paint; (2) once these tests are completed, and before any additional work is done, a site visit be organized for the Conservation Advisory Group to view the different tests and discuss the proposed procedures; (3) if it is determined that the black paint cannot be removed safely, a new restoration "bronze" surface will be applied to the black paint in a manner that rni1 1ics the original bronze surface; ( 4) if it is determined that the black paint can be removed safely, but the original surface has excessive loss, a barrier layer that protects and isolates what remains of the original surface from any added restoration surface will be applied to the original finish before an additional finish be added~ (5) if it is determined that the black paint can be removed safely and there is not excessive loss, the surface should be inpainted using a medium different from the original finish; and (6) the chronology should include more detailed information, such as exact dates for all of the past work and consultations, especially on the last page. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon the commencement of work before February I I, 2010.

Approval is given with the understanding that (1) the louvers will be dark (either charcoal grey or black), so they recede; (2) a single sheet of a translucent material, such as polycarbonate or Ecoresin, will be used instead of the glass block; (3) samples of any materials not being replaced in-kind will be submitted for review; and (4) if possible, a plan to visually integrate the lawn area on the interior of the smart fence with the park, perhaps by planting wildflowers and low-mow grass, will be developed in coordination with the Parks Department. Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before October 5, 2011 and submission of a minimum of three (3) 8" x 1 0" color archival-quality photographs of the completed project.

subject: the installation of The Coffee Cup bicycle rack by David Byrne, Amsterdam Avenue between 11 0'" Street and 111 '" Street, Manhattan

Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before February 1, 2012 and submission of a minimum of three (3) 8" x 1 0" color archival-quality photographs of the completed project.

subject: the relocation and reconstruction of a playground, Francis Lewis Park, Third Avenue, 1471h Street, the East River and Parsons Boulevard, Queens
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the relocation and reconstruction of a playground, Francis Lewis Park, Third Avenue, 1471h Street, the East River and Parsons Boulevard, Queens, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 2259-R, S, T & U of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that (1) archeological monitoring specifications will be included in the contract, and an archeologist would be on site to supervise all excavation and trenching in the existing soil; (2) air spades will be used to excavate as pipes go through the critical root zones of multiple trees; (3) the black cherry, which is a prolific reseeder, will be replaced with a more valuable species; (4) the benches will be studied to ensure there is an adequate number; (5) the designer will restudy the design (not the siting) of the playground, including the bridge and play equipment, so it is less generic; and (6) revised drawings reflecting these changes will be submitted for committee review before final designs are developed. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before December 13, 2012.

subject: the reconstruction of the Riegelmann Boardwalk, Phase II, Brighton Beach, Brighton 15th Street to Coney Island Avenue, Brooklyn
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the reconstruction of the Riegelmann Boardwalk, Phase II, Brighton Beach, Brighton 15th Street to Coney Island Avenue, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 1170-GR, GS & GU of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval. Given the negative impact of deforestation on the environment, the Commission supports the use of sustainable materials, but recognizes that this is a transitional period. Consequently, approval is given with the understanding that the Parks Department will continue to (1) monitor the installation of the high friction coefficient recycled plastic lumber, and report back to the Commission on its findings; (2) continue to work with manufacturers to increase recycled plastic lumber's friction coefficient and develop alternative sustainable materials; (3) continue to pursue Black Locust, including exploring setting up its own Black Locust farm; (4) narrow the concrete lane to 1 0' (from 12'); (5) study moving the concrete lane inboard, and submit an alternative design(s) for committee review; and (6) test potential wood alternatives on this section of the boardwalk. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for final review and approval before March 12, 2014.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the installation of an artwork by Matthew Geller, Myrtle Avenue Plaza, Myrtle Avenue between Hall Street and Emerson Place, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Cultural Affairs' Percent for Art Program, the Department of Design and Construction, and the Department of Transportation, represented by exhibits 6606-1, J & V of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval noting that, while this may be a welcome departure for the artist, the artwork will be a public statement of his work in New York City, and therefore must retain the fundamentals of the found object, which is essential to his work, and couple the elegance of the form with the rawness of the materials. Approval is given with the understanding that (1) the work will read more as an inverted manhole cover than a rose window; (2) the glass palette will be rich and not generic; {3) the colors will be distributed unevenly (contrary to the renderings), noting the importance of choosing a fabrication process that allows for idiosyncrasies in the glass form; (4) the shape of the top of the piece, including the glass, will be designed, so it does not trap water or debris such as leaves; and (5) rougher materials (cast iron and Cor-ten) will be used. Conceptual approval is conditioned upon submission of this project for preliminary review and approval before June 4, 2014.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the long-term loan of Civic Virtue (1922) by Frederick MacMonnies, Queens Borough Hall, southeast corner of Queens Boulevard and 801h Avenue, Queens, to Green-Wood Cemetery, Meadow Avenue and Garland Avenue, Brooklyn, submitted by the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, represented by exhibits 822-AQ, AR & AS of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary approval with the understanding that (1) the architect will continue to study the new base; (2) a proposal for the conservation of the sculpture will be submitted as soon as a conservator is selected (treatment will be undertaken after the sculpture is installed); and (3) landscape designs for the Queens Borough Hall site will be submitted for review in the next six months. Commissioner Pearsall recused himself. The Commission notes that Green-Wood Cemetery is a National Historic Landmark with one of the largest outdoor collections of 19th_ and 201h-century statuary and mausoleums, including the monument to James Wall Finn (1916) by Frederick MacMonnies. It is regularly open to the public and hosts tours and events to educate the public on its collections. In addition, several members of the MacMonnies family are interred at Green-Wood, and Frederick MacMonnies was to have been interred there, although plans changed after his death and he was interred elsewhere. The Commission thanks Green-Wood Cemetery for its generous support of the relocation of Civic Virtue, its stabilization and conservation, and its ongoing care while at Green-Wood. Preliminary approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before November 13, 2014 and submission of this project for final review and approval.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered a proposal for the replication of José Martí (1958) by Anna Vaughn Hyatt Huntington, Central Park, Manhattan, submitted by the Department of Parks & Recreation, represented by exhibits 3190-H & I of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous conceptual approval with the understanding that: (1) before this project returns for preliminary review, (a) a draft legal agreement between DPR and the Bronx Museum will be submitted to the Design Commission for review, (b) a final signed legal agreement will be submitted to the Design Commission for the file, and (c) the applicant will provide the name and credentials of the conservator who will oversee the scanning; (2) given that the sculpture has not been conserved since 1992 and the coatings are failing, a complete independent condition assessment will be done and a conservation proposal will be submitted to the Design Commission for review and approval; (3) in addition to the text on the base, the replica will be clearly marked as a reproduction in the bronze and the text must be submitted for Design Commission review; (4) after the reproduction is made, all molds will be destroyed and evidence of the destruction will be submitted for inclusion in the Design Commission archives; and (5) after the reproduction is made, all digital files will be provided to DPR. subject: the construction of a prototypical ambulance pedestal, Phase I, for installation citywide
resolution: RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered designs for the construction of a prototypical ambulance pedestal, Phase I, for installation citywide, submitted by the Fire Department, represented by exhibits 6816-FO & FP of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary and final approval with the understanding that (1) the lighting colors will be restudied and coordinated to ensure clear messaging; (2) FDNY will submit a revised color scheme for review before the pedestal design is completed; (3) the 30 individual pedestal locations will (a) comply with the approved siting guidelines, (b) be approved by DOT’s revocable consent division and the community board, and (c) be submitted for the Design Commission archive; (4) any installation that deviates from the approved siting guidelines will be submitted for review before the pedestal is installed; and (5) if FDNY expands the program to include more than 30 sites, the project will be resubmitted for committee review. Members commended the initiative and the design, noting an appreciation for the attention to detail. Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before May 2, 2018 and submission of comprehensive photographic documentation of the completed project consisting of 8” x 10” archival-quality color photographs.

RESOLVED That the Design Commission, having considered the design of prototypical public communications structures (Link5G) in Residence Zoning and Historic Districts, Phase I pilot, for installation citywide, submitted by the Office of Technology and Innovation, represented by exhibits 6816-JB & JC of record in this matter, hereby gives to the same unanimous preliminary and final approval to 200 Link5G pole installations citywide, noting that each pole must have at least one carrier in-contract before installation, and for poles located in Historic Districts, the Landmarks Preservation Commission has jurisdiction over the siting of the poles. Approval is given with the understanding that the team will (1) update the tablet interface to (a) indicate free Wi-Fi and 5G service capabilities and (b) allow the public to provide feedback on the design of the poles and service; (2) provide details on the community reception of the poles, including the design and provisioning of service; (3) include a decal with a symbol on the pole to indicate the 5G and/or Wi-Fi service and ensure that the sticker is re-applied if removed; (4) submit local and global examples of multi-tenant 5G pole structures sited on sidewalks in comparable dense urban neighborhoods with the goal of suggesting alternatives for a pole design in Residence Zoning and Historic Districts; and (5) remove and replace the pilot installations in the event another design is selected for citywide installation in Residence Zoning and Historic Districts. The Commission notes that the overall program will provide free Wi-Fi and 5G mobile carrier service to neighborhoods that are underserved, and any additional poles above this Phase I pilot for 200 poles must be submitted for review, per standard procedure. Final approval is conditioned upon commencement of work before September 12, 2024 and submission of comprehensive photographic documentation of the completed project consisting of 8” x 10” archival-quality color photographs.
